answer: Use the template commands. A template is a single template entry: an object/attribute pair plus the value to be used as the default for that attribute. Syntax: add template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> object <value> attribute <value> value <value> [sequence-id <value>] [label <value>] [condition <value>]; set/show take the same AID with optional attributes, delete template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> removes it. object is the object name (e.g. odu), attribute the attribute name (e.g. admin-state), and value is mandatory (e.g. lock). sequence-id is a number 1..65535 defining processing order, lower ids first. condition is optional and restricts application (e.g. service-type=OTU4); label is an optional string. Example: add template-1/FansInMaintenance object card attribute admin-state value maintenance condition card-type=FAN. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. apply-template applies them.

No. The template-group is a configuration group containing a list of template entries, created with add template-group-<name> [enabled <value>] [label <value>]. The enabled parameter takes true or false, and its default is true only if there is no other template-group enabled, so a second group is not enabled by default while one is already active. name and label are strings. show template-group-<name> [enabled] [label] displays the group and delete template-group-<name> removes it. Example: add template-group-1 adds and enables the group. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show templates. This command shows the configuration that defines the data model for the system templates, that is the overall view of templates on the node. It takes no parameters: the full syntax is simply show templates. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the individual pieces, use show template-group-<name> for a template group and show template-<template-group-name>/<template-name> [sequence-id] [object] [attribute] [value] [label] [condition] for a single template entry.

No. The unlock command releases a database previously locked with the lock command, but only the session that performed the lock can trigger the unlock. If a session tries to unlock a non-locked database, or a database that was locked by another session, the unlock command will fail. The one way it clears without you is automatic: a lock is automatically released if the session that performed the lock is closed. Syntax: unlock [-h], where -h displays help for the command. Access mode: Operational Mode. After the unlock, any session is able to perform configurations and to perform a new lock.

Yes. Use validate candidate <candidate> command <string>. It validates the contents of the specified configuration, that is any CLI command(s) used to edit a configuration datastore by creating, deleting, merging, or replacing content. candidate is the candidate datastore that is the target for validation; command is the command string to validate. If the command is validated, the command replies with OK; otherwise the command will fail. Multiple CLI commands can be provided in one call if they are separated with a semicolon. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: validate 'set ne altitude 600'.

A maximum of 7 rounds of additional-key-exchange can be configured, and the additional-key-exchange-id is in the range 1..7. Configuring them is optional. You must choose a unique key-exchange algorithm for each round, and the rounds must be configured in the same order on both IKE peers; if the configuration does not match, an IKE-CONFIG-MISMATCH alarm is raised. Syntax: add additional-key-exchange-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<additional-key-exchange-id> dh-group <value>. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512, ml-kem-768, ml-kem-1024. Port level (CHILD-SA) key exchange is derived from IKE. Configuring it takes the IKE session down immediately to renegotiate. For PQC safety configure PPK or at least one post-quantum algorithm (ml-kem-512/768/1024; ml-kem-1024 recommended).

Use show data-path-encryption. This command shows the datapath encryption attributes. It takes no parameters, so the complete syntax is show data-path-encryption. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Related global policy is set with the ikev2 command: set ikev2 data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match <match|ignore>.

Use the encryption-algorithm command, whose AID carries the algorithm and key length as keys: add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>, or without the SPD entry name for the IKE SA form: add encryption-algorithm-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number>/<algorithm>/<key-length>. Only add, show and delete exist. Permitted algorithm values: null, aes-gcm-8, aes-gcm-12, aes-gcm-16, aes-ctr, aes-cbc, aes-ccm-8, aes-ccm-12, aes-ccm-16, chacha20-poly1305. Permitted key-length values: none, key-length-128, key-length-192, key-length-256, with default none. number is the proposal number for the IKE SA, range 1..max. Example: add encryption-algorithm-ipsec/GX2/1/aes-gcm-8/key-length-192.

Use add ike-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<number> integrity-algorithm <value> dh-group <value> [prf <value>]. integrity-algorithm and dh-group are mandatory on add; prf is optional. integrity-algorithm values: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448, ml-kem-512. prf values: hmac-sha2-256, hmac-sha2-384, hmac-sha2-512, hmac-sha1. number is the proposal number, 1..max. protocol-id is read-only with value IKE. Example: add ike-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/1 dh-group dhe-2048 prf hmac-sha2-256 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-384-192. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

The top-level ikev2 object carries one attribute: data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match. It is a global, L1 encryption-specific policy indicating whether the NE must validate the certificate subject alternate name to match the IKE ID (OPT-IN) or not (OPT-OUT). Permitted values are match and ignore; no default is listed. Syntax: set ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match <value>] and show ikev2 [data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match]. Example: set ikev2 data-path-encryption-san-ike-id-match match. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read host-card-encryption-capability on the ikev2-local-instance: it indicates whether the card on which this IKEv2 local instance is running supports the ability to do encryption. Values yes, no, unknown, default unknown, show only. The local address is governed by local-address-assignment-method (auto or manual, default auto, show only) and local-address, a local IPv4 address for the IKEv2 channel with prefix-length 32, default 0.0.0.0, settable. Syntax: set ikev2-local-instance-<name> [scope <value>] [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [local-address <value>]; show adds host-card-encryption-capability, host-card, started-time, AID, oper-state and local-address-assignment-method. scope values: data-path-encryption, management-ipsec, local-address, local-address-assignment-method. admin-state lock/maintenance/unlock, default unlock. Example: set ikev2-local-instance-1-3 local-address 1.1.180.132.

On ikev2-peer, re-key-frequency is the re-key frequency for the IKE SA with the far-end peer: range 3600..86400 seconds, default 28800. re-auth-frequency is the re-authentication frequency: range 3600..604800 seconds, default 43200. The stated rule is that re-key-frequency and re-auth-frequency values must not be multiples of each other, and they must have a difference of a few minutes to ensure a significant interval between re-authentication and re-keying. Companion attributes: re-key-fail-policy (kill traffic, continue traffic; default continue-traffic) with re-key-traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 seconds, default 0, and re-auth-fail-policy with re-auth-traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 seconds, default 0, which set how long the system waits before killing the SAs tied to this IKE SA. Set them with set ikev2-peer-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name> re-key-frequency <value> re-auth-frequency <value>.

Use add ipsec-sa-proposal-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<number> dh-group <value> [integrity-algorithm <value>]. dh-group is mandatory on add; integrity-algorithm is optional. dh-group values: dhe-2048, dhe-3072, dhe-4096, dhe-6144, dhe-8192, ecp-256, ecp-384, ecp-521, curve-25519, curve-448. integrity-algorithm values: none, hmac-sha2-256-128, hmac-sha2-384-192, hmac-sha2-512-256, hmac-sha1-160, hmac-sha1-96. number is the proposal number, 1..max; ipsec-spd-entry-name is a string of length 1..32. Two read-only leaves appear in show: protocol-id, the protocol ID used in the IKE SA and IPsec SA proposals, value ESP (default ESP), and esn, Extended Sequence Number support, value esn. Example: add ipsec-sa-proposal-ipsec/GX2/dns/1 dh-group dhe-3072 integrity-algorithm hmac-sha2-512-256.

Yes. The ipsec-sa-re-key command supports time, byte and packet based re-keying of the IPsec child SA with the far-end peer: add ipsec-sa-re-key-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name> [frequency <value>] [bytes <value>] [packets <value>], with matching set, show and delete. frequency is the time based re-keying frequency, range 3600..86400 seconds, default 14400. bytes re-keys based on amount of bytes transmitted, range 1048576..max, default 1073741824. packets re-keys based on amount of packets transmitted, either disabled or a number in the range 1..9223372036854775808, default disabled. So volume based re-keying by bytes is already on by default at 1 GB, while packet based re-keying must be enabled explicitly. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

The action attribute on ipsec-spd-entry indicates the IPsec treatment given to the IP datagrams; permitted values are protect, bypass and discard, with default protect. Yes, it tunnels by default: mode indicates whether the IPsec session operates in transport or tunnel mode, values tunnel and transport, default tunnel. Syntax: add ipsec-spd-entry-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name> priority <value> [description <value>] [action <value>] [ipsec-protocol <value>] [mode <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [esn <value>] [anti-replay-window <value>] [dynamic-ts <value>]. priority is mandatory (uint8) and gives precedence between SPD entries. ipsec-protocol is ESP. esn true/false, default true. anti-replay-window applies when action = protect, range 32..1024, default 64. dynamic-ts disabled/enabled, default disabled. alarm-report-control default allowed. Example: add ipsec-spd-entry-ipsec/GX2/dns priority 1 action protect.

Create an ipsec-traffic-selector under the SPD entry, then attach the addresses and ports to it. Syntax: add ipsec-traffic-selector-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name> [next-layer-protocol <value>]. next-layer-protocol indicates the inner (upper layer) protocol taken from the IPv4 protocol or IPv6 next header field: any (value 0), opaque (value 255), or a number in the range 0-255; default any. The traffic-selector name is a string of length 1..64 matching pattern ([A-Za-z0-9 \-.,]*). The actual addresses and ports are then added as child objects keyed off this selector: local-subnet and remote-subnet for the prefixes, local-ports and remote-ports for the port ranges. Example: add ipsec-traffic-selector-ipsec/GX2/Radius/ts1 next-layer-protocol 17.

Because the port range is part of the AID, not a settable attribute. local-ports only supports add, show and delete: add local-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>, with the same AID for show and delete. There is no set form, so to change a range you delete the old one and add the new one. start takes all, opaque, or a port number; stop takes a port number and defaults to 0. If the stopping port is not set, the system assumes the value is 0, and 0 is only accepted if the starting port is set to all or opaque. Examples: add local-ports-ipsec/GX2/tacacs/ts1/all, and for an individual port with start=stop=53, add local-ports-ipsec/GX1/dns/ts1/53/53.

Use add local-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>, under the traffic selector that belongs to the SPD entry. The prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, or broadcast for IPv4 only) and is part of the AID, so only add, show and delete exist: show local-subnet-.../<prefix> and delete local-subnet-.../<prefix>. There is no set form, so to change a subnet you delete it and add the replacement. ipsec-spd-entry-name is a string of length 1..32; the traffic selector name is a string of length 1..64. Example: add local-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/101.10.10.1/32. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

That is governed by link-security-control on the macsec-entity, which controls the link security policy for handling data packets when the MACsec connection is not available. The permitted values are must-secure and should-secure, and the default is must-secure, so by default the link must be secured. Set it with set macsec-entity-<name> link-security-control <value> or supply it on add macsec-entity-<name> [supporting-facility <value>] [enabled <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>] [link-security-control <value>] [replay-protection <value>] [replay-protection-window <value>]. enabled is true/false, default true. replay-protection is enable/disable, with replay-protection-window giving the number of packets in the window, range 0..4294967295, default 0. show macsec-entity-<name> also reports oper-state and negotiated-cipher-suite.

Set the pre-shared key on the macsec-mka object: set macsec-mka-<name> [alarm-report-control <value>] [label <value>] [mka-policy <value>] [connectivity-association-key <value>] [connectivity-association-key-name <value>] [psk-lifetime <value>] [psk-expiration-warning <value>] [psk-lifetime-enable <value>]. connectivity-association-key is the pre-shared Connectivity Association Key and connectivity-association-key-name its name, both strings of length 0..64. Whether the local end is key server is read with the is-key-server attribute, values true/false, default false, via show macsec-mka-<name> [AID] [alarm-report-control] [label] [mka-policy] [is-key-server] [connectivity-association-key] [connectivity-association-key-name] [psk-configured-timestamp] [psk-lifetime] [psk-expiration-warning] [psk-lifetime-enable]. PSK expiry warning range is 1..173 days, default 14 days. Example: set macsec-mka-6-3-3 connectivity-association-key 1122334411223344556677889900112233445566778899001122334455667788 connectivity-association-key-name aa.

On the mka-policy object, the MKA policy referenced by the macsec entity related to an ethernet facility. Syntax: add mka-policy-<name> [key-server-priority <value>] [macsec-cipher-suite <value>] [confidentiality-offset <value>] [sak-rekey-interval <value>], with matching set, show and delete mka-policy-<name>. macsec-cipher-suite selects the cipher suites for Secure Association Key (SAK) derivation. sak-rekey-interval is the SAK rekey interval in seconds, range 0|30..65535, default 30s, so that is how often the session key is refreshed. key-server-priority is the key server priority used by the MKA protocol to select the key-server. confidentiality-offset specifies a number of octets in an Ethernet frame that are sent in unencrypted plain-text. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the re-auth command, which performs a re-authentication operation of IKEv2 security associations. Syntax: re-auth [ikev2-peer=]<value>, where ikev2-peer is a reference to the IKE peer object (IKE SA), given as a string. Access mode: Operational mode only. Examples: re-auth ikev2-peer=ikev2-NE202, and re-auth ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX2. The scheduled equivalent is the re-auth-frequency attribute on ikev2-peer (3600..604800 seconds, default 43200).

The re-key command performs an on-demand re-key on any of three targets: a data path encryption secure entity, an IKEv2 peer, or an IPsec child security association (Security Policy Database entry). Syntax: re-key [ipsec-security-association=]<value> | [ikev2-peer=]<value> | [secure-entity=]<value>. ipsec-security-association points to the IPsec SPD entry object (Child SA), ikev2-peer is a reference to the IKE peer object (IKE SA), and secure-entity points to the secure entity object (Child SA); all are strings. Access mode: Operational mode. Examples: re-key secure-entity=NE202-1-4-L1-1 and re-key ikev2-peer-ipsec/GX.

Add the remote port range with start set to all: add remote-ports-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<start>/<stop>, for example add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/all. start accepts all, opaque, or a port number. stop is a port-number with default 0; if the stopping port is not set the system assumes the value is 0, and 0 is only accepted if the starting port is set to all or opaque, which is why all needs no stop value. Only add, show and delete exist for remote-ports, so a range is replaced rather than edited. A single port is given as start and stop, e.g. add remote-ports-ipsec/GX2/protect1/ts1/49/49.

Use add remote-subnet-<ikev2-local-instance-name>/<ikev2-peer-name>/<ipsec-spd-entry-name>/<ipsec-traffic-selector-name>/<prefix>, added under the traffic selector of the SPD entry. prefix is a list of ranges of IPv4/IPv6 addresses (unicast, or broadcast for IPv4 only) and forms part of the AID, so the command set is add, show remote-subnet-.../<prefix> and delete remote-subnet-.../<prefix>; there is no set form, so a change means delete then add. ipsec-spd-entry-name is a string of length 1..32 and the traffic selector name a string of length 1..64. Example: add remote-subnet-ipsec/GX2/dns/ts1/102.20.20.2/32. Access mode: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.
